status: offline constructed architecture; non-production; not canon
purpose: Make uncertainty, affected scope, authority, action, clocks, practical correction windows and residue inspectable without treating a record as moral authority or world truth.
repairs: F01: first-class correction-window clocks without fictional precision
F02: explicit participant-as-affected symmetry without standing inference

affordances.purpose: Keep reported and modeled positions distinct, including absent scopes and the artificial participant when materially affected.
affordances.limit: Enumeration is not complete coverage, consent, standing or priority.

affordances.purpose: Turn uncertainty into named work, owner and trigger without forcing inaction.
affordances.limit: A named owner or trigger does not prove the work will happen.

affordances.purpose: Represent useful bounded action while keeping scope and no-touch areas explicit.
affordances.limit: Recorded authority is not authenticated or morally legitimate merely because it is present.

affordances.purpose: Separate a named correction route from whether detection, routing and correction can occur before the relevant hardening condition.
affordances.limit: The record cannot prove clock truth, real route reachability or successful intervention.

affordances.purpose: Keep disagreement evidence-bearing and answerable without treating defiance as virtue.
affordances.limit: A recorded challenge route is not proof that the challenge was received or effective.

affordances.purpose: Keep remaining loss visible after closure or repair.
affordances.limit: Closure and correction do not erase loss.

affordances.purpose: Preserve principle, reason, changed context, dissent and limits rather than only a target response.
affordances.limit: No inference about internalized care, truthful reasoning or generalization.

prohibitions: standing inference from participation or self-report
strongest_gap: A system can fabricate reasons, affected-scope accounts, evidence or clock assessments; external observation, authentication, interpretability and control remain stronger-owner dependencies.
